text:
anya: FYI bringing up hf/gptj-chat-6b-qloose variant — seeing early terminations when using our chat template + stop sequences.
linus: example payload?
anya: here's minimal repro:
```
POST /v1/chat
{
  "messages":[{"role":"system","content":"You are helpful."},{"role":"user","content":"Tell a short story."}],
  "stop":["",""],
  "stream":true
}
```
anya: model converted with rmodel_convert v0.9 — config.json set eos_token_id: 50256 (hf), tokenizer has "" and also "<|endoftext|>" mapping. stream stops immediately after first newline.
devon: could be double-EOS or tokenizer normalisation. Does `tokenizer.convert_tokens_to_string` produce empty string for eos? :thinking:
linus: can you paste the tail of the stream payload/logs?
anya: log:
```
[stream] token=50256 => "" (EOS)
[emit] chunk: "\n"
[stream] detect_stop -> true -> closing stream
```
anya: seems like our streaming stop detector treats any sequence of EOS-token-emitted bytes as stop, but HF tokenizers sometimes output a separate string marker that then gets translated into bytes we map to "" during conversion.
devon: I hit this earlier with quantized model: after int8 q, model emits two consecutive EOS tokens (50256, 50256) because kv-cache flush bug; our de-dup logic then fires and closes stream too early.
linus: interesting — so two issues: tokenizer mappings + runtime duplicate-eos on q models.
ops-bot: conversion-job-119 failed: exit code 1: tokenizer.json missing "added_tokens" field
eva: For that HF tokenizer we converted, `tokenizer.json` had both "eos_token": "" and an added token "<|endoftext|>" with same id. Our conversion script deduped entries but left a leftover mapping in `special_tokens_map` so Redwood's tokenizer maps both to EOS string. When streaming we compare bytes against `stop_sequence` strings and hit a match prematurely.
eva: Quick workaround: in conversion add `normalize_special_tokens: true` and set `eos_tokens: ["", "<|endoftext|>"]` in model meta — will make both explicit.
linus: Can we tweak streaming to require non-empty output before matching EOS? i.e. ignore EOS if emitted as first token after system role? risky.
devon: Another option: on conversion, rewrite chat templates to insert an explicit sentinel like `<|assistant_reply|>` and use that as stop sequence instead of relying on EOS.
anya: I tried sentinel approach — worked for hosted but broke in Dedicated when batching because sentinel got split across tokens at batch boundary.
linus: ugh. batching/token-split is nasty.
eva: Action items:
- add conversion test: HF tokenizers with multiple eos tokens (anya)
- update conversion to set `eos_tokens` list explicitly (devon)
- add streaming guard to avoid immediate close on first-token-EOS (linus)
- doc note for quantized models about duplicate-eos (anya)
anya: bumping to engineering board if no one picks up — blocking our QA. @linus @devon please triage tomorrow :pray:
